P1.summary: Support article presents a single simplified formula for Order Margin regardless of order type/side, while SoT specifies four distinct formulas (buy limit, buy market, sell limit, sell market) with different price inputs including BestBid comparisons for sell orders.

P1.supportQuote: Currently, no. Delta Exchange does not have a native iOS or Android App. We do however offer a Progressive Web App (PWA).
P1.sotQuote:
On Delta Exchange app
Go to Trade and in the next screen click on Basket Order
P1.summary: Support article states no native iOS or Android app exists, but the guides describe a native app workflow for placing basket orders, directly contradicting the claim.

P1.supportQuote: Lets say you have a long position of 1000 lots in the BTCUSD Perpetual contract on Delta Exchange. Recall that the lot size of the BTCUSD Perpetual is 0.001 BTC.
P1.sotQuote: Lets say you have a long position of 1000 contracts in the BTCUSDT Perpetual contract on Delta Exchange. Recall that 1 BTCUSDT contract is 0.001BTC.
P1.summary: Support article uses 'BTCUSD Perpetual' and the term 'lots' in the funding example, while the guides use 'BTCUSDT Perpetual' and 'contracts', suggesting either a different contract or outdated terminology in the support article.

P1.supportQuote: BNBUSDQBinance Coin - USD QuantoVanilla Future, quoted in USD, settled and margined in BTC
P1.sotQuote: ETHUSDQEthereum - USD QuantoVanilla Future, quoted in USD, settled and margined in USDC ... XRPUSDQRipple - USD QuantoVanilla Future, quoted in USD, settled and margined in USDC
P1.summary: The support article is internally inconsistent: BNBUSDQ is listed as settled in BTC while other USDQ contracts (ETHUSDQ, XRPUSDQ, LTCUSDQ) are listed as settled in USDC, and the article also describes BSVUSDQ as settled in BTC despite the 'Q' suffix implying USDC settlement like the others.

P1.supportQuote: Endpoint: /v2/tickers/{symbol} ... This powerful endpoint delivers comprehensive market data for a specific trading pair
P1.sotQuote: GET /tickers ... This endpoint retrieves the live tickers for available trading products, with an optional filter by specified contract types.
P1.summary: Support article describes the Tickers API only as a per-symbol endpoint (/v2/tickers/{symbol}), omitting the bulk /v2/tickers endpoint that retrieves all tickers with optional contract_type filtering, which is documented in the India docs.

P1.supportQuote: we will provide advance notifications to users regarding scheduled maintenance via our official Twitter, Telegram channel, and the in-app notification (bell icon)
P1.sotQuote: We will announce any scheduled maintenance at least 24 hours in advance.
P1.summary: The support article lists notification channels (Twitter, Telegram, in-app bell) but omits the SoT's explicit requirement that scheduled maintenance be announced at least 24 hours in advance.

P1.supportQuote: Phase 2 (Auction Mode): Place, modify, or cancel limit orders; Make deposits and withdrawals
P1.sotQuote: Step 1: Market is put into post-only mode. Traders are able to post and/ or cancel limit orders. However, at this time, orders are not matched.
P1.summary: Support article calls the post-maintenance limited mode 'Auction Mode' and says deposits/withdrawals are available during it, but the SoT describes it as 'post-only mode' with no mention of deposits/withdrawals being re-enabled at that stage.

P1.supportQuote: If the IOC order is filled at a price better than the Implied Bankruptcy Price, a liquidation charge is deducted from the position margin assigned to the PPL.
P1.sotQuote: If the IOC order is filled at a price better than the Implied Bankruptcy Price, a liquidation charge (equaling Maintenance Margin_min) is deducted from the position margin assigned to the PPL.
P1.summary: The support article omits the specific definition of the liquidation charge as equaling Maintenance Margin_min, which the guides explicitly state, leaving users without the precise formula.

P1.supportQuote: Check the X-Rate-Limit-Remaining header to monitor your usage.
P1.sotQuote: 'X-RATE-LIMIT-RESET' is returned in response header with time left in milliseconds after which next API request can be hit.
P1.summary: Support article says to check 'X-Rate-Limit-Remaining' header to monitor usage, but Delta Exchange docs indicate the relevant header returned is 'X-RATE-LIMIT-RESET' (time until reset), not a remaining-count header.

P1.supportQuote: liquidation process stops as soon as a state is achieved in which collateral available for margining is more than the initial
P1.sotQuote: Immediately after the Liquidation engine is done executing the above-mentioned trades, the portfolio is checked for margin sufficiency, i.e. is the initial margin required for the new portfolio is less than the available collateral. If yes, liquidation process stops.
P1.summary: Support article's liquidation section is truncated and does not describe the full iterative loop (repeat steps 2 and/or 3 until sufficiently margined or completely liquidated) that the SoT guides describe.

P1.supportQuote: IOC orders are always executed as taker orders and hence incur taker fees.
P1.sotQuote: All market orders are by default marked as IOC. Limit orders can be marked as IOC to guarantee immediate execution at the specified price or better.
P1.summary: Support claims IOC orders always incur taker fees, but SoT indicates limit orders can also be marked IOC — a limit IOC that posts and fills as maker would not necessarily incur taker fees, making the blanket taker-fee claim potentially incorrect.

P1.supportQuote: Locate and click on the main portfolio tab available on the extreme right of your Delta Exchange India account
P1.sotQuote: You can change the margin mode of an account/ sub-account from the margin mode selector on the top of the order placement panel or from the sub-account management page.
P1.summary: Support article describes accessing margin mode change via a 'portfolio tab on the extreme right', while SoT states the margin mode selector is at the top of the order placement panel or the sub-account management page.

P1.supportQuote:
For a short position in a Futures contract:
PnL=−n∗m∗(1/Fut_EntryPrice−1/Fut_CurrentPrice) (in BTC)
P1.sotQuote:
For a short position in a Futures contract:
PnL=−n∗m∗(1/Fut_EntryPrice−1/Fut_CurrentPrice) (in BTC)
P1.summary: The support article presents the short position unrealised PnL formula using the inverse futures formula (1/price terms) under the vanilla futures section, which matches the guides verbatim but is contextually misleading — the guides clearly separate vanilla and inverse futures PnL formulas, while the support article conflates them by placing the inverse-style short formula under the vanilla futures PnL section without distinguishing contract type.

P1.supportQuote: The current method was made effective from 5:30pm IST on the 8-Sep-2025 to make funding more predictable, easier to track and in line with global best practices.
P1.sotQuote: The current method was made effective from 12pm UTC on the 8-Sep-2025 to make funding more predictable, easier to track and in line with global best practices.
P1.summary: Support article states the new funding method took effect at 5:30 pm IST on 8-Sep-2025, while the guides state 12pm UTC on the same date — 12pm UTC is 5:30 pm IST, so these are actually equivalent; however the support article uses IST and guides use UTC, which is consistent with the broader time-zone discrepancy pattern and should be verified.

P1.supportQuote: Tickers are now in format: < option_type > - < asset > - < strike > - < expirydate in ddmmyy >
P1.sotQuote: Option Type |-| Underlying Asset |-| Price Strikes |-| Expiry Date in ddMMYY e.g. C-BTC-90000-310125
P1.summary: Support article describes the expiry date format as 'ddmmyy' (all lowercase), while docs.delta.exchange specifies 'ddMMYY' (mixed case), suggesting the month component is two-digit uppercase — a minor but potentially confusing format discrepancy for API users.

P1.supportQuote: IOC orders are always executed as taker orders and hence incur taker fees.
P1.sotQuote: Limit orders can be marked as IOC to guarantee immediate execution at the specified price or better. However, if the order cannot be filled completely, the unfilled portion will be cancelled.
P1.summary: Support article states IOC orders always incur taker fees, but the SoT guides make no such claim for limit IOC orders; a limit IOC order that rests momentarily could execute as maker, and the SoT does not restrict IOC to taker-only execution.

P1.supportQuote: Multiple timeframe options (1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 1d, 7d, 30d, 1w, 2w)
P1.sotQuote: GET /tickers/{symbol} ... The symbol(s) of the product, comma-separated. Maximum 10 symbols allowed.
P1.summary: Support article lists '7d' and '2w' as valid Historical Data API resolution options alongside standard intervals; these non-standard resolutions are not confirmed in the India developer docs and may be inaccurate for the India platform.

P1.supportQuote: In case the position is not fully liquidated (for example due to lack of liquidity), an off market trade for the remaining position is executed at the Bankruptcy Price between the trader and the Liquidation Engine.
P1.sotQuote: In case the ICO order is not fully filled, an off market trade at the Implied Bankruptcy Price of the PPL is executed between the trader and the Liquidation Engine.
P1.summary: The support article lists the incremental liquidation step about the off-market trade before the step about the IOC fill outcome, whereas the guides list the fill-better-than-bankruptcy step before the not-fully-filled step, reversing the order of the two incremental liquidation sub-steps.

P1.supportQuote: The take-profit order is an order that is triggered at a predefined level and aims to lock in profits.
P1.sotQuote: The take-profit order is a market order which is triggered at a pre-defined level and aims to lock-in profits. And, the stoploss order is a stop market order to limit losses.
P1.summary: Support article describes bracket order take-profit as a generic 'order' and lists multiple take-profit/stop-loss subtypes, while the guides describe bracket take-profit specifically as a market order and stop-loss as a stop market order only; the support article's expanded subtype list (take-profit limit, stop-loss limit, trailing) may conflict with the guides' narrower definition of bracket order components.

P1.supportQuote: Go to API Keys
P1.sotQuote: You can create a new API key from here : https://www.delta.exchange/app/account/manageapikeys
P1.summary: Support article says to navigate to 'API Keys' but docs specify the path as 'account/manageapikeys'; the docs also refer to this section as 'API Management' not 'API Keys'.

P1.supportQuote: the take-profit and stop-loss orders become active as soon as the main order is executed
P1.sotQuote: the take-profit and stoploss orders are placed in the order book as soon as the main order is executed
P1.summary: Support says bracket sub-orders 'become active' when the main order executes, while the guides say they are 'placed in the order book' — the guides' phrasing implies they are immediately live orders, whereas 'become active' could imply a triggered/conditional state, a potentially misleading distinction for users.

P2.supportQuote: Note that the status field shows the current system state (in this case "api_fallback"), while the event field indicates that maintenance was cancelled.
P2.sotQuote:
"status": "api_fallback", // current status
"event":"maintenance_cancelled"
P2.summary: Support article prose correctly says 'api_fallback' but the JSON payload above it uses 'api-fallback' (hyphen), creating an internal inconsistency that contradicts the docs canonical value.

P2.supportQuote: Trigger Condition: The order is triggered only when the Mark Price reaches the Stop Price you define.
P2.sotQuote: Trigger Price can be based off one of the three price indices: (a) Mark Price, (b) Last Traded Price, or (c) Index Price (i.e. price of the contract's underlying). By default, Mark Price is used as the Triggering Index.
P2.summary: The support article states only Mark Price is used as the trigger condition, omitting that Last Traded Price and Index Price are also valid triggering indices (Mark Price is merely the default).

P2.supportQuote: Only the Mark Price can be used as the triggering index for bracket orders.
P2.sotQuote: bracket_stop_trigger_method: stop order trigger method for bracket orders- mark_price/last_traded_price/spot_price
P2.summary: Support article restricts bracket order trigger to Mark Price only, but the CreateBracketOrderRequest schema in docs explicitly enumerates mark_price, last_traded_price, and spot_price as valid values.

P2.supportQuote: PnL calculations are illustrated with examples in the Options and Futures guide section.
P2.sotQuote: PnL calculations are illustrated with examples in the PnL Math section.
P2.summary: Support article references 'Options and Futures guide section' for PnL examples, but the authoritative guide references the 'PnL Math section' as the correct location.

P2.supportQuote: The Settlement Price, also known as the ending price, is the 30 minute TWAP of the underlying asset - Bitcoin or Ethereum - at time of settlement. The absolute movement of the underlying asset at settlement time is therefore settlement price - strike price.
P2.sotQuote: SettlementPrice=abs(Ending Price−Starting Price)
P2.summary: Support article defines the absolute movement as 'settlement price - strike price' (a simple subtraction), but the SoT guide specifies it is the absolute value of (Ending Price − Starting Price), i.e. abs(), which is materially different for direction of movement.

P2.supportQuote: The order activates only when the Mark Price reaches your specified Stop Price.
P2.sotQuote: Trigger Price can be based off one of the three price indices: (a) Mark Price, (b) Last Traded Price, or (c) Index Price (i.e. price of the contract's underlying). By default, Mark Price is used as the Triggering Index.
P2.summary: Support article states the order activates only when Mark Price reaches the stop price, omitting that Last Traded Price and Index Price are also valid triggering indices, which could mislead users into thinking Mark Price is the only option.

P2.supportQuote: Only the Mark Price can be used as the triggering index for bracket orders.
P2.sotQuote: bracket_stop_trigger_method: stop order trigger method for bracket orders - mark_price/last_traded_price/spot_price
P2.summary: Support article states only Mark Price can be used as the triggering index for bracket orders, but the API docs show bracket_stop_trigger_method accepts mark_price, last_traded_price, or spot_price.

P2.supportQuote: Basket orders are supported for portfolio margin.
P2.sotQuote: Isolated Margin: Each position is completely independent and the total margin required will be equal to the sum of the margin for each position. Cross Margin: The initial margin will be either same or lower than the margin required for Isolated Margin.
P2.summary: The support article states basket orders are supported only for portfolio margin, but the SoT guide explicitly describes margin behaviour for basket orders under Isolated Margin and Cross Margin as well, indicating basket orders are available across all margin modes.

P2.supportQuote: At Delta Exchange, we offer call and put options on BTC and ETH. All these are European options (i.e. they can only be exercised on expiry) and are available for a multitude of strikes and expiry dates.
P2.sotQuote: At Delta Exchange, we offer the following four categories of options contracts: Vanilla Options ... Option Spreads ... MOVE Options ... Turbo Options (deprecated)
P2.summary: The support article describes only vanilla call and put options on BTC and ETH, omitting the other categories of options contracts (Option Spreads, MOVE Options) that the guides explicitly list as available products.

P2.supportQuote: ProductSymbol: specifies which product category a given contract belongs to. Currently, it can take the following values: C (Call), P (Put)
P2.sotQuote: ProductSymbol ... C Call, TC Turbo Call, P Put, TP Turbo Put, MV MOVE
P2.summary: Support article only lists C and P as valid ProductSymbol values, omitting TC (Turbo Call), TP (Turbo Put), and MV (MOVE) which are listed in the guides (even if Turbo is deprecated, MV/MOVE is not marked deprecated).

P2.supportQuote: ensuring that traders pay the maker fee upon submission
P2.sotQuote: the traders will earn a maker rebate when the order is executed.
P2.summary: Support article says post-only orders ensure traders 'pay the maker fee', but the guides state traders 'earn a maker rebate' — these describe opposite financial outcomes for the same fee type.

P2.supportQuote: A limit order is an order to buy a specified number of futures contracts at a specified price.
P2.sotQuote: A limit order is an order to buy or sell a specified number of futures contracts at a specified price.
P2.summary: Support article defines a limit order only as an order to 'buy', omitting 'sell', whereas the SoT explicitly states it is an order to 'buy or sell'.

P2.supportQuote: Currently, we offer options on BTC and ETH.
P2.sotQuote: Currently, we offer options on BTC, ETH, BNB, LINK, XRP, LTC, BCH, SOL and ADA.
P2.summary: Support article lists only BTC and ETH as underlying assets for options, while the guides list a broader set including BNB, LINK, XRP, LTC, BCH, SOL, and ADA.

P2.supportQuote: you can choose either Isolated Margin or Cross Margin, depending on your preference
P2.sotQuote: Delta Exchange offers three margin modes: Isolated Margin, Portfolio Margin, Cross Margin
P2.summary: Support article lists only two margin modes (Isolated and Cross) as selectable options, omitting Portfolio Margin as a third available mode.

P2.supportQuote: Scheduled maintenance (typically 6-24 hours' advance notice)
P2.sotQuote: We will announce any scheduled maintenance at least 24 hours in advance.
P2.summary: Support article states advance notice is 'typically 6-24 hours', but the official guides state the minimum is 'at least 24 hours' in advance, making the 6-hour lower bound inconsistent with the stated policy.

P2.supportQuote: Order Margin = Order Size * Notional Value of 1 contract x Initial Margin%
P2.sotQuote: Buy limit order: IM = (Initial Margin% * #Contracts * Multiplier * Limit_Bid_Price); Buy market order: IM = (InitialMargin% * #Contracts * Multiplier * MarkPrice)
P2.summary: Support article gives a single simplified IM formula using 'Notional Value of 1 contract', whereas the SoT guide provides distinct formulas for buy/sell limit/market orders that differ by price reference (Limit_Bid_Price, MarkPrice, BestBid), omitting the order-type distinction entirely.

P2.supportQuote: We have also discontinued Turbo Options.
P2.sotQuote: Turbo Options (deprecated) ... Turbo options are exotic options in which a knockout barrier is attached to vanilla call/ put options.
P2.summary: Support article says Turbo Options are 'discontinued', while guides.delta.exchange labels them only as 'deprecated' and still retains full documentation for them, creating ambiguity about their actual status (SoT appears outdated — needs update).

P2.supportQuote: All Orders on Delta Exchange are traded on Isolated Margin.
P2.sotQuote: Delta Exchange offers three margin modes: Isolated Margin, Portfolio Margin, Cross Margin
P2.summary: Support article claims all orders use Isolated Margin exclusively, but SoT confirms Delta Exchange also supports Portfolio Margin and Cross Margin modes, making the blanket statement inaccurate.

P2.supportQuote: The default time in force flag for market orders... is GTC (Good till cancelled).
P2.sotQuote: All market orders are by default marked as IOC.
P2.summary: The SoT guides state market orders are by default marked as IOC, while the SoT's Allowed Trading Bands page states the default TIF for market orders is GTC — this is a guides-internal inconsistency also relevant to the support article's omission of market order default behaviour.

P2.supportQuote: When the Mark Price hits the stop price, a market order is triggered.
P2.sotQuote: Trigger Price can be based off one of the three price indices: (a) Mark Price, (b) Last Traded Price, or (c) Index Price (i.e. price of the contract's underlying). By default, Mark Price is used as the Triggering Index.
P2.summary: The support article presents Mark Price as the sole trigger method for trailing-stop orders, but the guides (and docs) confirm that Last Traded Price and Index Price are also valid trigger methods, with Mark Price being only the default.

P2.supportQuote: In this margining method, margin is shared between open positions and orders.
P2.sotQuote: In this margining method, margin is shared between open positions and orders. In cross margin, each position/ order is allocated the minimum margin required to keep the position/ order open. This means that all positions and orders are opened/ kept at the highest allowed leverage.
P2.summary: The support article omits the key detail that in cross margin, positions/orders are always opened at the highest allowed leverage, which is a material characteristic of how cross margin works.

P2.supportQuote: The margin requirement for a portfolio with offsetting positions (e.g. futures/ options spreads) is likely to be much lower... In such cases, you may need to close all the margined positions together
P2.sotQuote: In such cases, you may need to close all or a group of the portfolio margined positions together. You can do this by placing a basket order
P2.summary: Support article omits the actionable guidance that users can close a group (not necessarily all) positions together via a basket order; it only says 'close all the margined positions together'.

P2.supportQuote: Below are the two different types of TIF Flags on Delta Exchange: Immediate or Cancel (IOC) ... Good till Cancelled (GTC)
P2.sotQuote: The default time in force flag for market orders as well as stop market orders is GTC (Good till cancelled)... you have the option to place IOC (immediate or cancel) market order and stop market orders.
P2.summary: Support article describes only two TIF flags (IOC and GTC) and does not mention that IOC can also be applied to market orders and stop market orders via API, omitting a material use case documented in SoT.

P2.supportQuote: The reason Open Orders on other contracts is not cancelled is that on Delta Exchange traders use Isolated Margin instead of Cross Margin.
P2.sotQuote: Only USDT settled futures and options contracts support Cross Margin mode
P2.summary: Support article implies Cross Margin is not available on Delta Exchange at all, but SoT confirms Cross Margin is a supported margin mode for USDT settled futures and options contracts.

P2.supportQuote: Below are the 2 different types of TIF Flags on Delta Exchange
P2.sotQuote:
Order Validity Attributes

Immediate or cancel (IOC)... Good till cancelled (GTC)... All market orders are by default marked as IOC.
P2.summary: Support article claims there are only 2 TIF flags (IOC and GTC), but the SoT guides also describe FOK is absent — more critically, the article title promises FOK coverage yet the body omits it entirely, and the SoT confirms market orders carry IOC by default as a third distinct TIF behaviour not covered.

P2.supportQuote: In the case of a single letter (Q) added post the quote currency, the letter represents the type of currency product.
P2.sotQuote: Underlying Asset| Quoting Asset|_|Matruity Date (optional, applicable only for futures contracts) e.g. BTCUSD, ETHUSD
P2.summary: Support article describes a 'Q' suffix in the symbology format to denote Quanto products, but the authoritative docs symbology section makes no mention of a Q suffix and only describes Underlying Asset + Quoting Asset + optional maturity date.

P2.supportQuote: It is a series of continuous payments that are exchanged between longs and shorts in a perpetual contract.
P2.sotQuote: We previously had a minute-by-minute funding exchange between longs and shorts. The current method was made effective from 12pm UTC on the 8-Sep-2025 to make funding more predictable, easier to track and in line with global best practices.
P2.summary: Support article describes funding as 'continuous payments' (implying minute-by-minute), but SoT clarifies the current method is periodic (8-hour intervals), not continuous minute-by-minute, as of 8-Sep-2025.

P2.supportQuote: The system shows the combined margin requirement before you place the basket order.
P2.sotQuote: Portfolio Margin: The risk of the whole basket is analysed together to compute the combined margin requirement for the entire group which provides the benefit of PnL and risk offsetting. Please note that this benefit is available only for market orders.
P2.summary: Support article states the combined margin is shown before placing the order without qualification, but SoT specifies that the portfolio margin benefit (combined/reduced margin calculation) is available only for market orders, not limit orders.

P2.supportQuote: Position that are held till maturity are cash settled at a price that is computed using the settlement method described in the contract specifications - https://www.delta.exchange/contracts.
P2.sotQuote: Position that are held till maturity are cash settled at a price that is computed using the settlement method described in the contract specifications.
P2.summary: Support article appends a hardcoded URL (https://www.delta.exchange/contracts) for contract specifications that is absent from the authoritative guide, which may be outdated or incorrect.

P2.supportQuote: The default time in force flag for market orders as well as stop market orders is GTC (Good till cancelled).
P2.sotQuote: The allowed trading band for interest rate swap (IRS) contracts is created by combining three different bands which are described below:
P2.summary: The support article omits the Interest Rate Swaps (IRS) section entirely, which is present in the guides SoT and describes a distinct three-band methodology for IRS contracts.

P2.supportQuote: Reduce-only is most useful when paired with stop orders, helping you: Close a position if the market moves against you. Prevent accidental over-leverage or overexposure.
P2.sotQuote: While the reduce only flag can be used with any order type, it is most useful when combined with stop orders.
P2.summary: Support article omits the SoT's explicit clarification that the reduce-only flag can be used with any order type, not just stop orders, which is a material omission that could limit users' understanding of the feature's applicability.

P2.supportQuote: Enable "Trading" permissions
P2.sotQuote: There are two permissions given 1. Read Data ✅ 2. Trading ✅
P2.summary: Support article instructs users to enable only 'Trading' permission, but docs indicate there are two distinct permissions ('Read Data' and 'Trading') and recommends granting only necessary ones; omitting 'Read Data' may cause issues for some AlgoTest operations.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Delta Exchange has two funding currencies - BTC and USDT. This means that you can deposit either bitcoins or Tether (USDT) to your Delta wallet
conflicts.docsQuote: Bitcoin Perpetual futures margined and settled in INR ... Ethereum perpetual futures margined and settled in INR
conflicts.summary: Guides describe BTC and USDT as funding/settling currencies, while docs explicitly state that India perpetuals (BTCUSD, ETHUSD) are margined and settled in INR, indicating the guides are stale with respect to the India platform.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Funding Rate is computed 3 times in a 24 hour period at: 8am UTC, 4pm UTC and 12am UTC. At these times, the TWAP of Premium in the preceding 8 hours is used to compute the Funding Rate. This Funding Rate thus obtained remains applicable for the next 8 hours.
conflicts.summary: The guides describe the funding rate computed at the end of each 8-hour window as applicable for the NEXT 8 hours, while the docs websocket response includes a 'next_funding_realization' (nfr) timestamp field suggesting the rate is realized at a future point — the two sources use different models (prospective vs. retrospective application) for when a computed funding rate takes effect, which could confuse API consumers.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Funding is exchanged between longs and shorts once every 8 hours at 8 am UTC, 4 pm UTC and 12am UTC.
conflicts.docsQuote: rate_exchange_interval: 28800 (The time interval, in seconds, at which funding rates are exchanged between long and short positions.)
conflicts.summary: Guides and docs agree that the rate_exchange_interval is 28800 seconds (8 hours), which is consistent; however, the guides' OTC section still states 'funding is exchanged between longs and shorts every minute' for OTC contracts, creating an internal guides inconsistency between standard and OTC perpetual funding exchange frequency.

conflicts.guidesQuote: All market orders are by default marked as IOC.
conflicts.docsQuote: The default time in force flag for market orders as well as stop market orders is GTC (Good till cancelled).
conflicts.summary: Two pages on guides.delta.exchange contradict each other on the default time-in-force for market orders: the Order Types page says market orders are IOC by default, while the Allowed Trading Bands page says the default is GTC.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Only Mark Price can be used as the Triggering Index for bracket orders.
conflicts.summary: Guides state only Mark Price can trigger bracket orders, but the API docs enumerate three valid trigger methods: mark_price, last_traded_price, and spot_price.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Only Mark Price can be used as the Triggering Index for bracket orders.
conflicts.docsQuote: bracket_stop_trigger_method: stop order trigger method for bracket orders - mark_price/last_traded_price/spot_price
conflicts.summary: Guides state that only Mark Price can trigger bracket orders, while the API docs expose bracket_stop_trigger_method accepting mark_price, last_traded_price, and spot_price — a direct conflict on the allowed trigger methods for bracket orders.

conflicts.guidesQuote: The default time in force flag for market orders as well as stop market orders is GTC (Good till cancelled).
conflicts.summary: One guides page says market orders default to GTC, while another guides page (Order Types) says all market orders are by default marked as IOC — these two guides pages directly contradict each other on the default TIF for market orders.

conflicts.guidesQuote: A bracket order lets a trader to 'bracket' any given order with two opposite-side orders, i.e. take-profit and stoploss order. The take-profit order is a market order which is triggered at a pre-defined level.
conflicts.summary: Guides describe the take-profit leg of a bracket order as always a market order, but the API docs show take_profit_order accepting order_type 'limit_order' with a limit_price, indicating limit orders are also supported for take-profit.

conflicts.guidesQuote: We currently offer two margin modes: isolated margin and portfolio margin.
conflicts.docsQuote: margin_mode: The target margin mode: 'isolated' or 'portfolio'. Enumerated Values: isolated, portfolio
conflicts.summary: The Margin Explainer guide lists three margin modes (Isolated, Portfolio, Cross), but the Market Makers guide and the API ChangeMarginModeRequest schema both enumerate only two modes (isolated and portfolio), omitting cross margin as a valid option.

conflicts.guidesQuote: ProductSymbol-UnderlyingSymbol-StrikePrice-ExpiryDate ... TC: Turbo Call, TP: Turbo Put
conflicts.docsQuote: Option Type |-| Underlying Asset |-| Price Strikes |-| Expiry Date in ddMMYY e.g. C-BTC-90000-310125
conflicts.summary: Guides list TC and TP as valid ProductSymbol values for Turbo Call and Turbo Put options in the symbology table, while docs.delta.exchange omits these entirely from the options symbol format, reflecting inconsistent treatment of deprecated Turbo Options across the two authoritative sources.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Funding Rate is computed 3 times in a 24 hour period at: 8am UTC, 4pm UTC and 12am UTC... Funding is exchanged between longs and shorts once every 8 hours at 8 am UTC, 4 pm UTC and 12am UTC.
